claims.text: Catalytic performance in ethanol oxidation over platinum-group-metal nanoscale catalysts is governed by synergy between the metal nanoparticles and oxygen vacancies in an adjacent oxide support.
Interfacial oxygen vacancies promote the formation of adsorbed hydroxyl groups.
Adsorbed hydroxyl groups facilitate ethanol dehydrogenation and oxidation of reaction intermediates.
The proposed vacancy-mediated process enhances ethanol-oxidation activity, selectivity toward complete oxidation to CO2, and catalyst durability.
Conventional solution-phase or impregnation synthesis followed by calcination produces supported Pt-group-metal nanoparticles with a low inherent oxygen-vacancy concentration.
Hydrogen reduction at 200–300 °C will increase the concentration of oxygen vacancies at metal-support interfaces.
The hydrogen-reduction treatment can create additional oxygen vacancies without significantly altering nanoparticle size.
The relevant structural mediator is the density of oxygen vacancies at the interface between the Pt-group-metal nanoparticles and the oxide support.
Vacancy-induced adsorbed hydroxyl groups react with adsorbed ethanol-derived intermediates.
Reaction of adsorbed hydroxyl groups with ethanol-derived intermediates mitigates catalyst poisoning.
Vacancy-induced hydroxyl groups lower the activation barrier for the 12-electron oxidation of ethanol to CO2.
Hydrogen-treated catalysts should exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than otherwise identically prepared untreated catalysts.
Hydrogen-treated catalysts should produce a greater proportion of CO2 relative to partial oxidation products.
Hydrogen-treated catalysts should exhibit greater operational durability during ethanol oxidation.
The mechanism applies when the oxide support remains stable and accessible for hydroxyl-group formation.
The mechanism may fail at very high electrode potentials where oxide dissolution occurs.
The mechanism may fail under extreme thermal conditions where sintering or other deactivation mechanisms dominate.
